content: 1. Glycopyrronium Tosylate (Topical) and Dimenhydrinate: The pharmacodynamic interaction between these two agents may lead to enhanced effects due to synergism. Co-administration with other anticholinergic medications can result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Gotu Kola and Dimenhydrinate: Gotu Kola may potentiate the effects of dimenhydrinate through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination may enhance central nervous system (CNS) depression. Exercise caution and monitor for signs of excessive sedation. 3. Dimenhydrinate and Haloperidol: Both drugs increase sedation when used together. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for excessive sedative effects. 4. Hawthorn and Dimenhydrinate: Hawthorn may enhance the effects of dimenhydrinate via pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 5. Hops and Dimenhydrinate: Hops can increase the effects of dimenhydrinate through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially leading to enhanced CNS depression. Monitor the patient closely. 6. Dimenhydrinate and Hyaluronidase: Dimenhydrinate may reduce the effects of hyaluronidase. Antihistamines, when administered in large systemic doses, can render tissues partially resistant to the action of hyaluronidase. Patients may require higher doses of hyaluronidase to achieve the desired dispersing effect. Use caution and monitor. 7. Dimenhydrinate and Hydromorphone: Co-administration of these drugs increases sedation. Use caution and monitor for excessive sedative effects. 8. Dimenhydrinate and Hydroxyzine: Both agents increase sedation when used together. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for signs of excessive sedation. 9. Dimenhydrinate and Iloperidone: The combination of these drugs increases sedation. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 10. Dimenhydrinate and Imipramine: Co-administration of these drugs results in increased sedation. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 11. Dimenhydrinate and IncobotulinumtoxinA: Dimenhydrinate enhances the effects of incobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Drugs with anticholinergic properties may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 12. Dimenhydrinate and Isoproterenol: Dimenhydrinate increases sedation, while isoproterenol decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor the patient. 13. Kava and Dimenhydrinate: Kava may enhance the effects of dimenhydrinate through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor for excessive sedation. 14. Ketamine and Dimenhydrinate: Both drugs increase sedation when used together. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 15. Dimenhydrinate and Ketotifen (Ophthalmic): Co-administration of these agents increases sedation. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 16. Lasmiditan and Dimenhydrinate: Either drug may increase the sedative effects of the other. Co-administration with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated in clinical studies. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 17. Lemborexant and Dimenhydrinate: Both drugs increase sedation when used together. Dosage adjustments may be necessary due to potentially additive effects. Monitor therapy closely. 18. Dimenhydrinate and LetibotulinumtoxinA: Dimenhydrinate enhances the effects of letibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Drugs with anticholinergic properties may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 19. Dimenhydrinate and Levalbuterol: Dimenhydrinate increases sedation, while levalbuterol decreases it. The overall effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor the patient. 20. Dimenhydrinate and Levetiracetam: Both drugs increase sedation when used together. Exercise caution and monitor for excessive sedative effects.
